question.:question/problem:
Find the equation of the normal line to the curve $y=- 3 x^{2} - 3$ at the point $(1,-6).$

$x\,-$
{{field-1}}$\cdot \,y\,=$
{{field-2}}
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $f(x)=- 3 x^{2} - 3.$ First, we compute the derivative:

$$
f'(x)=\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}\left(- 3 x^{2} - 3\right)=- 6 x
$$

Then, we compute the slope of the tangent at the point $(1,-6):$

$$
m=f'(1)=-6
$$

Therefore, the slope of the normal line is

$$
m'=-\frac{1}{m}=\frac{1}{6}.
$$

Finally, the equation of the normal line is

$$
\begin{aligned}y-(-6)&=\frac{1}{6}(x-(1)) \\ x - 6 y&=37.\end{aligned}
$$

Find the equation of the normal line to the curve $y=\frac{x^{6}}{8} - \frac{5 x^{3}}{4} - 1$ at the point $(1,- \frac{17}{8}).$

$x\,-$
{{field-1}}$\cdot \,y\,=$
{{field-2}}
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $f(x)=\frac{x^{6}}{8} - \frac{5 x^{3}}{4} - 1.$ First, we compute the derivative:

$$
f'(x)=\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}\left(\frac{x^{6}}{8} - \frac{5 x^{3}}{4} - 1\right)=\frac{3 x^{5}}{4} - \frac{15 x^{2}}{4}
$$

Then, we compute the slope of the tangent at the point $(1,- \frac{17}{8}):$

$$
m=f'(1)=-3
$$

Therefore, the slope of the normal line is

$$
m'=-\frac{1}{m}=\frac{1}{3}.
$$

Finally, the equation of the normal line is

$$
\begin{aligned}y-(- \frac{17}{8})&=\frac{1}{3}(x-(1)) \\ x - 3 y&=\frac{59}{8}.\end{aligned}
$$

Find the equation of the normal line to the curve $y=\frac{x^{6}}{4} - \frac{5 x^{3}}{4} - 1$ at the point $(1,-2).$

$x\,-$
{{field-1}}$\cdot \,y\,=$
{{field-2}}
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $f(x)=\frac{x^{6}}{4} - \frac{5 x^{3}}{4} - 1.$ First, we compute the derivative:

$$
f'(x)=\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}\left(\frac{x^{6}}{4} - \frac{5 x^{3}}{4} - 1\right)=\frac{3 x^{5}}{2} - \frac{15 x^{2}}{4}
$$

Then, we compute the slope of the tangent at the point $(1,-2):$

$$
m=f'(1)=- \frac{9}{4}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the normal line is

$$
m'=-\frac{1}{m}=\frac{4}{9}.
$$

Finally, the equation of the normal line is

$$
\begin{aligned}y-(-2)&=\frac{4}{9}(x-(1)) \\ x - \frac{9 y}{4}&=\frac{11}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $f(x)=\frac{1}{8}{x}^{6}-\frac{7}{4}{x}^{3}+1.$ First, we compute the derivative:

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{1}{8}{x}^{6}-\frac{7}{4}{x}^{3}+1)=\frac{3}{4}{x}^{5}-\frac{21}{4}{x}^{2}
$$

Then, we compute the slope of the tangent at the point $(2,-5):$

$$
m={f}^{′}(2)=\frac{3}{4}({2}^{5})-\frac{21}{4}({2}^{2})=3
$$

Therefore, the slope of the normal line is

$$
{m}^{′}=-\frac{1}{m}=-\frac{1}{3}.
$$

Finally, the equation of the normal line is

$$
\begin{aligned}y-(-5) & =-\frac{1}{3}\cdot (x-2) \\ -3(y-(-5)) & =x-2 \\ - 3 y - 15 & =x-2 \\ x+3\cdot y & =-13.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: The equation of the normal line to the curve $y=2{x}^{5}-2x-2$ at the point $(1,-2)$ is given by $y=ax+b$ where $a$ and $b$ are constants. Find the value of $a+b.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $f(x)=2{x}^{5}-2x-2.$ First, we compute the derivative:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) &=\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2{x}^{5}-2x-2)=10{x}^{4}-2\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we compute the slope of the tangent at the point $(1,-2):$

$$
\begin{aligned}m &={f}^{′}(1)=10(1)^{4}-2=8\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the normal line ${m}^{′}$ is

$$
{m}^{′}=-\frac{1}{m}=-\frac{1}{8}.
$$

Finally, the equation of the normal line is

$$
\begin{aligned}y-(-2) & =-\frac{1}{8}(x-1) \\ y & =- \frac{x}{8} - \frac{15}{8}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $a+b=- \frac{1}{8}+(- \frac{15}{8})=-2.$

question.:question/problem: The equation of the normal line to the curve $y=\frac{4}{\sqrt{x}}$ at the point $(1,4)$ is given by $x+py=q$ where $p$ and $q$ are constants. Find the value of $q-p.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $f(x)=\frac{4}{\sqrt{x}}.$ First, we compute the derivative:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{4}{\sqrt{x}}) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(4{x}^{-1/2}) \\  & =-2{x}^{-3/2} \\  & =-\frac{2}{\sqrt{{x}^{3}}}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we compute the slope of the tangent at the point $(1,4):$

$$
\begin{aligned}m &={f}^{′}(1)=-\frac{2}{\sqrt{{1}^{3}}}=-2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the normal line ${m}^{′}$ is

$$
{m}^{′}=-\frac{1}{m}=\frac{1}{2}.
$$

Finally, the equation of the normal line is

$$
\begin{aligned}y-4 & =\frac{1}{2}(x-1) \\ 2y-8 & =x-1 \\ x-2y & =-7.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $q-p=-7-(-2)=-5.$

question.:question/problem: The equation of the normal line to the curve $y=\frac{4}{{x}^{2}}-x$ at the point $(1,3)$ is given by $x+py=q$ where $p$ and $q$ are constants. Find the value of $p-q.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $f(x)=\frac{4}{{x}^{2}}-x.$ First, we compute the derivative:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{4}{{x}^{2}}-x) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(4{x}^{-2}-x) \\  & =-8{x}^{-3}-1\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we compute the slope of the tangent at the point $(1,3):$

$$
\begin{aligned}m &={f}^{′}(1)=-8(1)^{-3}-1=-9\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the normal line ${m}^{′}$ is

$$
{m}^{′}=-\frac{1}{m}=\frac{1}{9}.
$$

Finally, the equation of the normal line is

$$
\begin{aligned}y-(3) & =\frac{1}{9}(x-1) \\ 9y-27 & =x-1 \\ x-9y & =-26.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $p-q=-9-(-26)=17.$
